origin.description: This function creates colors of class HSV; a subclass of the virtual color class.

arguments.name: H, S, V
arguments.text: Hue, saturation, and value. Separate vectors or a three-column matrix passed as H.

arguments.name: names
arguments.text: Row names for the colors. By default the row names of H are used.

origin.details: Hues should lie between 0 and 360; saturation and value between 0 and 1. HSV is a relative color space derived from RGB. Conversion to another space goes through a specific RGB space such as sRGB.
origin.value: An object of class HSV which inherits from class color. The coords slot is a matrix with columns H, S, and V.

translation.description: This function creates colors of class HSV; a subclass of the virtual color class.

arguments.name: H, S, V
arguments.text: Hue, saturation, and value as separate arrays or scalars, or an n by 3 matrix as H when S and V are omitted. Scalars for S or V recycle to the length of H.

arguments.name: names
arguments.text: Row names. When H is a (matrix, rownames) pair, row names default from the pair if names is omitted.

translation.details: Hues should lie between 0 and 360; saturation and value between 0 and 1. Calling HSV() with no H returns an empty HSV object. A matrix that is not n by 3, or a length mismatch after recycling, raises invalid color matrix.
translation.value: An HSVColor object. space is HSV, coords is an n by 3 float64 array with columns H, S, and V, and names is the row names or None.
translation.example:
from colorspace.hsv import HSV
import numpy as np

print(HSV(np.linspace(0, 360, 13)[:-1], 1, 1))
